entities.summary: Fred Jay Seaver was an American mycologist. He worked at the New York Botanical Garden for 40 years, initially as the Director of Laboratories (1908–1911), then as the Curator (1912–1943), and finally as Head Curator (1943–1948). Between 1907 and 1909 he issued two exsiccatae, North Dakota Fungi and Ascomycetes and lower fungi, the later with G. W. Wilson. He was also an editor of the journal Mycologia between 1909 and 1947. In 1928, Seaver published North American Cup-fungi (Operculates), which was expanded with a supplement in 1942 and a second volume in 1951, titled North American Cup-fungi (Inoperculates).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Fred Jay Seaver's work on North American Cup-fungi (Operculates) contributed significantly to mycological research and understanding of fungal diversity in North America. His publications had a lasting impact on the field, with his second volume remaining an important resource for researchers.
